headline: Climeworks reports Mammoth DAC plant captured six times more CO₂ in H1 2026 as running costs more than halve
summary: Climeworks said its Mammoth direct-air-capture plant in Iceland removed 675 tonnes of CO₂ in the first half of 2026 — almost six times the year-earlier figure — with the cost of running the plant down by more than half, on plant-design and filter-material upgrades.
co2crc_note: DAC cost-down and throughput scaling is a durable-CDR trajectory signal CO2CRC tracks for technology benchmarking.
extractor_note: 675 t is a half-year (H1 2026) removal figure, not nameplate annual capacity, so capacity_mtpa left null.

headline: Vateris secures over €50m in binding offtakes and LOIs for CO₂-derived carbon-negative minerals
summary: UK climate-tech firm Vateris signed binding multi-year offtake agreements and letters of intent worth over €50m in potential annual turnover with six industrial partners (Holcim, Marshalls and Goldbeck for GypCarb calcium carbonate; Waypoint Commodities and two fertiliser producers for sulphate of potash), mineralising captured flue-gas CO₂ into construction materials and fertiliser; first deliveries from a UK demonstration plant from late 2027.
co2crc_note: Demand-side signal for CO₂ utilisation/mineralisation offtakes and CBAM-driven European low-carbon supply chains.
extractor_note: €50m is potential annual offtake turnover (mix of binding agreements and LOIs), not a discrete CCS funding commitment, so amount left null.

headline: Finland awards €26.6m to three industrial biogenic carbon-capture (BECCS) projects
summary: Finland's Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment awarded €26.6m in state investment aid to three industrial biogenic carbon-capture projects — €21m to Metsä Fibre for a 100,000 t/yr biogenic CO₂ capture unit at its Rauma pulp mill — the first awards under a €90m competitive scheme, with the captured biogenic CO₂ destined largely as feedstock for e-fuels.
organisations: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (Finland)
co2crc_note: European BECCS state-aid precedent; biogenic CO₂-to-e-fuels pathway relevant to durable-removal policy design.
extractor_note: Award decision dated 9 Sep 2026 — outside the 10–11 Sep briefing window, carried as radar; follows the 4 Sep Ministerial Finance Committee endorsement. capacity_mtpa 0.1 is the Metsä Fibre unit only, not the three-project total.
